issues.description: Conflicting specification for the SealSaloon.stock attribute: The problem statement (lines 70-72) instructs that the SealSaloon's attributes (orders and stock) "should be initialized to default values ... in the constructor of SealSaloon" (implying stock is an instance field initialized in the instance constructor). Later in the same problem statement (lines 77-81) it explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and lists methods related to the shared stock as static. The reference solution (SealSaloon.java line 5) implements stock as a static final field initialized at declaration. This contradiction (instance vs. static/shared) in the exercise description will confuse students about whether to implement stock as an instance field initialized in the constructor or as a static field initialized at declaration or in a static initializer.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the requirement consistent: either (A) require stock to be an instance field and keep the instruction to initialize it in the no-arg constructor, or (B) require stock to be a shared static field and update the text to say the shared static stock must be declared static (e.g. 'private static final Stock stock = new Stock();') and initialized at declaration or in a static initializer (not in the instance constructor). Update the UML/text accordingly so all places consistently specify the same design. Prefer option B if you want a shared stock as in the reference solution; explicitly state "stock is static (shared across instances) and should be initialized at declaration (or in a static initializer)".
